  Friday, January 30, 2026, 7:30 AM - Saturday, January 31, 2026, 3:30 PM, University
  of Washington | Tower, Seattle, WA <div>Credits</div> <em>AMA PRA Category 1 Credits™</em>
  (9.75 hours), Non-Physician (9.75 hours) <div>Target Audience</div> <div> <em>Professions</em>
  - Naturopathic Physician, Non-Physician, Nurse, Nurse Practitioner, Pharmacist,
  Physician, Physician Associate, Student, Technician</div> <div>Overview</div> <p>Men
  are disproportionately afflicted by urologic disease, and “Men’s Health” is an established
  medical arena where specialized knowledge is required. The diagnosis and management
  of men’s health diseases are continually evolving and are heavily influenced by
  advances in diagnostic technology, medications, and surgical devices. The greatest
  challenge that care providers face is staying up to date with the changes in this
  field, thereby assuring state-of-the-art care for their patients. Expert faculty
  have been assembled to provide this update, with presentations on topics such as
  prostate screening and treatment, testosterone deficiency, male urinary dysfunction,
  kidney and bladder pathology, sexual dysfunction, male infertility, and genital
  pain syndromes. After the plenary sessions, attendees will have the opportunity
  to participate in question &amp; answer sessions.</p> <p><b><em><span>PROGRAM VENUE: </span></em></b>University
  of Washington Tower   Tower Auditorium4333 Brooklyn Ave NESeattle, WA 98195</p>
  <div>Objectives</div> <div><p>At the end of this program learners will be able to:</p></div>
  <ol> <li>Associate the role of PSA screening in men and describe additional tests
  now available for prostate cancer screening and diagnosis.</li> <li>Extrapolate
  a more holistic approach to men''s health including the complex interplay between
  common comorbidities.</li> <li>Illustrate the management options for men with localized
  prostate cancer, including active surveillance.</li> <li>Give examples of the quality-of-life
  issues men face after prostate cancer treatment and develop a paradigm for addressing
  common issues.</li> <li>Interpret diagnostic criteria in the evaluation of men with
  microscopic and gross hematuria.</li> <li>Outline the appropriate methods of evaluation
  for men suspected of having hypogonadism and discuss the risks and benefits of testosterone
  treatment.</li> <li>Distinguish the relationship between cardiovascular disease
  and erectile dysfunction and offer appropriate treatment options to men experiencing
  ED and other forms of sexual dysfunction.</li> <li>Point out the association between
  male infertility and disease, and discuss the evidence-based evaluation of male
  infertility.</li> <li>Classify the key elements of a BPH evaluation and provide
  appropriate treatment options.</li> <li>Generate the appropriate evaluation of men
  with scrotal content pain and discuss and evidence-based initial treatment approach.</li>
  <li>Explain the approach to evaluating chronic male genitourinary pain and the various
  treatment options available.</li> </ol> <div>Registration</div> <p> </p> <p><strong><em><span>Registration

  content=\"University of Washington School of Medicine, 11th Annual Men&#39;s Health
  Update (MJ2610), 1/30/2026 7:30:00 AM - 1/31/2026 3:30:00 PM, &lt;p>Men are disproportionately
  afflicted by urologic disease, and “Men’s Health” is an established medical\narena
  where specialized knowledge is required. The diagnosis and management of men’s health\ndiseases
  are continually evolving and are heavily influenced by advances in diagnostic technology,\nmedications,
  and surgical devices. The greatest challenge that care providers face is staying
  up to date\nwith the changes in this field, thereby assuring state-of-the-art care
  for their patients. Expert faculty\nhave been assembled to provide this update,
  with presentations on topics such as prostate screening\nand treatment, testosterone
  deficiency, male urinary dysfunction, kidney and bladder pathology, sexual\ndysfunction,
  male infertility, and genital pain syndromes. After the plenary sessions, attendees
  will have\nthe opportunity to participate in question &amp;amp; answer sessions.&lt;/p>&lt;p>&lt;b>&lt;em>&lt;span
  style=&quot;color: rgb(112, 48, 160);&quot;>PROGRAM VENUE:&amp;nbsp;&lt;br>&lt;/span>&lt;/em>&lt;/b>University
  of Washington Tower&amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp;&lt;br>Tower Auditorium&lt;br>4333 Brooklyn
  Ave NE&lt;br>Seattle, WA 98195&lt;/p>\" /><meta name=\"keywords\" content=\"Continuing
  Medical Education, CME, University of Washington School of Medicine, 11th Annual
  Men&#39;s Health Update (MJ2610)\" /></head>\r\n<body>\r\n    <!-- Notification

source_url: https://uw.cloud-cme.com/course/courseoverview?EID=13842&P=5
start_date: '2026-01-30T08:00:00-08:00'
summarized: true
title: 11th Annual Men's Health Update
topic_titles:
- Health Care
---

Join the 11th Annual Men's Health Update on January 30-31, 2026, at the University of Washington Tower in Seattle. This two-day event focuses on the evolving diagnosis and management of men’s health issues, particularly urologic diseases. Attendees can expect expert-led presentations on a variety of topics, including prostate screening, testosterone deficiency, male urinary dysfunction, and sexual health. The program features interactive Q&A sessions, allowing participants to engage directly with specialists. This event is designed for healthcare professionals, including physicians, nurses, and pharmacists, offering up to 9.75 AMA PRA Category 1 Credits™. Registration is now open, with early bird pricing available until October 31, 2025. Don’t miss the opportunity to enhance your knowledge and improve patient care in this critical area of health.
